subject: NovusAI pilot: observability plan & success gates
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Feb 2028 15:22:00 -0500
Subject: NovusAI pilot: observability plan & success gates

Hi Julia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps for the pilot so we have alignment on scope, metrics, and ownership before we kick off the PoC: 

Summary of ask
- 3-week pilot to validate inference economics and visibility for our recommender model (sequence length ~512, bursty traffic).
- Primary goals: baseline latency under 90ms p50, traceable 99th percentile under 600ms, and raw-token cost reduction target (>=15%) using caching/quantization suggestions.

Proposed observability scope (what Redwood will deliver)
- Dashboards: p50/p95/p99 latency per model, token throughput, request/second, batch size distribution, tail latency by input-size bucket.
- Tracing: end-to-end traces in Jaeger-compatible spans with sampling policy and root-cause tags (model, region, batch_id).
- Logs: structured logs exported to your S3 (daily partitions) and a CloudWatch mirror for alerts. Logs will include request_id, model_version, prompt_hash (hashed), kv_cache_hits.
- Metrics: token-generation rate, cache-hit ratio, requeue/drop counts, GPU utilization, queue depth, and inference error rate (4xx/5xx).

Success criteria (minimal pass)
- Functional: Redwood serves production-weighted requests without errors for at least 48 hours of steady traffic.
- Performance: p50 < 90ms, p95 < 400ms for the canonical workload; p99 < 600ms for 95% of test runs.
- Observability: All dashboards populated and traces correlate to 90% of slow requests; logs available in S3 with 7-day retention.

Timeline & owners
- Week 0 (this week): instrument mapping + S3 destination + access (owner: NovusAI infra – Marcus).
- Week 1: deploy PoC config + initial dashboard + smoke test (owner: Neha/Redwood).
- Week 2: focused load runs, tracing taps, and remediation tuning (owner: NovusAI + Redwood ops).
- Week 3: evaluation run, report, and decision (owner: Julia/NovusAI with Neha supporting).

Attachments: I attached a short requirements spreadsheet with the mapping fields we need for logs and a one-page evaluation checklist.

Can you confirm Marcus and any security contacts who should get S3 write credentials? Once I have names I’ll share a minimal IAM policy.

Thanks,

On Fri, Feb 9, 2028 at 3:22 PM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick recap + proposed next steps for the pilot so we have alignment on scope, metrics, and ownership before we kick off the PoC:

Thanks Neha — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed owners: Marcus (infra) will own S3/IAM; I’ll own evaluation decisions with product stakeholders (Priya + Omar). Security will need the log schema and retention policy before we sign off.
- We want traces to include a request_type tag (interactive vs. batch) and the prompt_hash must be salted on our side — we can provide the salt to Redwood via a secure secret.
- For the cost target, we prefer to measure token cost per 10K inferred tokens rather than a percentage in initial runs.

Can Ben or Lauren advise if Redwood can add a simple alert for token-spike anomalies (threshold-based) and a playbook for investigating spikes? Marcus, can you confirm your S3 bucket name and whether a cross-account role is preferred?

Julia Park
Head of Product, NovusAI
julia@novusai.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Bell <marcus@novusai.com>, NovusAI Security <security@novusai.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Feb 2028 08:43:00 -0500
Subject: Re: NovusAI pilot: observability plan & success gates

Thanks Julia — great notes. Short replies inline and updates below.

> Traces: include request_type tag and salted prompt_hash
Yes — we’ll add request_type span tag and support an externally supplied salt for prompt hashing. We will never log raw prompt content.

> Token cost metric per 10K tokens
Done — we’ll report token_cost_per_10k as part of the evaluation dashboard.

> Alerts for token-spike anomalies + playbook
Ben — can you own the alert template and a one-page investigation playbook? Suggested alert triggers: 3x baseline token rate sustained for 3 minutes, sudden batch-size collapse, or cache-hit drop >40%.

Marcus — can you share the bucket name or confirm cross-account role preference? If you want a role, we will provide a sample IAM role ARN to attach.

Updated timeline (minor tweak):
- Wed (Day 0): Marcus provides S3/role + security gives log schema approval.
- Fri (Day 2): Redwood deploys PoC config; we run smoke tests.
- Day 6–10: Load + tracing enabled; weekly sync.
- Day 17: Final evaluation + summary.

I have attached the requirements spreadsheet and a printable checklist for your product team.

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 13 Feb 2028 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: NovusAI pilot: observability plan & success gates

Thanks — happy to take the alert/playbook. I’ll draft a short runbook with three investigation paths (network, serving runtime, and client payload) and an alert bundle you can import directly into PagerDuty/Datadog.

Quick note on retention: Our default PoC retention for logs is 14 days (configurable); if security needs 7 days we can reduce, but we recommend 14 during the pilot for debugging.

I’ll post the alert templates and a link to the runbook to the shared drive by end of day.

-Ben
